title: Scones
tagline: A deliciously simple recipe for the novice, the dabbler and the seasoned baker alike!
byline: A family recipe contributed by Emily Bell.
ingredients: 1 cup lemonade or tonic water
method: Sift the flour into a bowl, then make a well and add the remaining ingredients and gently mix together until the mixture just comes together as a dough.
Dust a clean surface with flour and roll out the dough until it's about 2cm thick.
Use a cookie cutter or other appropriately sized object to cut out scones.
Bake in an oven heated to 200°C fan force for 15–20 minutes.

title: Choconut Bikkies
tagline: These dark and indulgent biscuits will turn you into a crunchy cookie monster. Not so sweet, but so good!
byline: A family recipe created by Rachel Hollingworth.
ingredients: 1⁄4 cup lightly packed brown sugar
1⁄4 cup chopped walnuts or pecans
1⁄2 cup rice flour + 1⁄2 cup corn flour, or 1 cup plain flour
method: Preheat oven to 170°C (150°C fan force). Line two baking trays with baking paper.
Place butter, golden syrup, honey and sugar in a small saucepan over a low-medium heat. Stir occasionally and remove from heat when butter is melted.
Add vanilla to saucepan, stir through and set aside.
Combine flour, rolled oats, desiccated coconut, brazil nuts, almonds, walnuts/pecans, pumpkin seeds, cocoa powder and cinnamon in a large mixing bowl.
Pour butter mixture into dry ingredients and mix.
Roll mixture into golf ball sized balls and slightly flatten onto baking trays.
Bake for approximately 10min, being careful not to over cook as they are quite dark.

title: Yellow Lentil Soup
tagline: This budget friendly comfort soup is great just by itself or with some freshly baked sourdough bread.
byline: A family recipe created by Rachel Hollingworth.
note: For those who just want/need it done with as little fuss as possible, follow step one, then throw all the other ingredients in and it will turn out just fine.
credit: Recipe inspired by Dari’s Lentil Soup and Iman’s Yellow Lentil Soup.
ingredients: 1⁄2 tsp cayenne pepper or chilli powder
10–12 cups stock (chicken, beef or vegetable)
method: In a large pot, over medium heat, cook the onions in the olive oil until translucent and slightly golden (around 15 minutes).

Add the crushed garlic and cook for another minute. Add the turmeric, cayenne pepper and cumin, cooking for another minute before adding in the stock (being sure to scrape the flavour from the bottom).

Add in the lentils, carrots and ginger. Reduce heat and leave to simmer, stirring occasionally, until everything is cooked and the soup has reduced a little (about an hour). If a thicker consistency is desired (which it generally is), leave on the heat for a while longer; if not, remove from heat and blend the soup until it is the desired consistency.
